text:
maria: FYI — ACME legal requires they keep all egress credentials in their own KMS for the private deployment. They want a handoff model where we never persist the secrets. Need to design an acceptance flow and surface edge cases. :thinking:

ajay: ok — do they want to push NAT IPs + BGP, or just hand us certs/tokens? any timeline?

maria: they want to provide: (1) egress NAT IP pool, (2) a service principal cert issued from their PKI, (3) KMS-managed signing key for service-to-service auth. timeline: onboarding sprint in 3 weeks.

devon: main concerns: rotation, failover, and testability. acceptance criteria we should require: short checklist.

leila: sketch of acceptance criteria (frontline):
- customer provides stable egress IP CIDR(s) that route to our edge (or BGP session)
- customer provides a public cert / CA bundle we can validate (no private key transfer)
- credential handshake API that accepts only ephemeral tokens, which we validate against their KMS via signed nonce
- rollback/fallback plan: if handshake fails we must safely fall back to a shared egress path under strict audit
- logging: every handshake attempt recorded with correlation id for audits

ajay: +1. Also want a small proto for handshake HTTP flow, e.g.:
```
POST /v1/egress/handoff
Headers: X-Corp-Nonce, Date
Body: {"signed_nonce": "<base64>", "egress_cidrs": ["1.2.3.0/24"]}
```
We then call their KMS cert endpoint to verify signature. We never store private material, only the verified fingerprint.

maria: ACME insists on us proving we never keep the key. They'll run an attestation. We should include an "ephemeral proof" protocol and a documented audit artifact.

devon: edge cases to call out in RFC:
- multi-region: customer may provide different egress pools per region; we need consistent routing + config drift checks
- time skew pushing signed_nonce validity window too tight -> onboarding flakiness
- partial failure: customer's KMS unreachable during rollout -> should auto-defer to canary route
- rotation: customer rotates signing key -> how do we handshake rekey without outage? need warming period + dual-key acceptance

leila: also: DNS resolution for service endpoints — if customer manages egress, they may expect us to use their forwarders. We need clear defaults and an opt-in for custom DNS.

product-ops: for launch gating, propose:
- must pass automated integration tests in staging (handshake happy path + 3 failure modes)
- SRE runbook complete and DR tested (can cut traffic to fallback path in <5m)
- legal sign-off on customer-provided key attestations
- monitoring: egress auth failure rate <0.1% over 24h prior to cutover

sre-bot: Incident policy attached: https://redwood-internal.local/policies/egress-handshake (auto-post) :robot_face:

ajay: next steps: I'll draft an RFC doc with the handshake API, sample flow, and acceptance checklist. Need volunteers for review: @maria (product), @devon (platform), @leila (sre).

maria: thanks — I'm available for design review tomorrow 10:30 PT. I'll ping ACME for precise KMS endpoints and their key rotation cadence. :thumbsup: 

devon: I'll start a small integration harness to simulate key rotation + KMS outages. plan to have a PoC by EOD Friday.

leila: I'll draft runbook snippets for fallback routing and validation steps.

product-ops: I'll add launch gate items to the checklist and own legal coordination.

maria: agreed — let's reconvene after the RFC draft. If anyone discovers any hard blocker (e.g., customer refuses to publish a CA bundle) call it out here ASAP.

(automated note) sre-bot: thread archived to eng-platform/rfcs after 7 days of inactivity.
